turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil sternly reminded Sandip that the threat was not an idle one, citing the recent clashes between Hindus and Mussulmans in neighboring villages.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil what steps he had taken to prevent such incidents from occurring in their own village.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip take the necessary precautions to ensure the safety of his villagers, lest they suffer the consequences of his inaction.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was being dramatic and that the local Mussulmans were hardly a threat, more like a nuisance, and that he had more pressing concerns than coddling his ego

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant attitude was a dereliction of duty and that he was putting the entire estate at risk with his carelessness

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip smirked and told Nikhil that he should be more concerned about his own crumbling estate, rather than lecturing him on duty

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his estate's current state was no excuse for neglecting his duties to the community, and that he would not be swayed by personal considerations when it came to the safety of the village.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and pointed out that Nikhil was always so concerned about the community's safety, but never about the state of their own crops, which were withering away before their very eyes.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his careless attitude towards the community's safety was a luxury he could ill afford, given the delicate balance of power in the region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted and retorted that Nikhil was just making a big fuss over nothing, that the Mussulmans were harmless and would never dare attack him, his family, or his precious estate.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil firmly insisted that Sandip's carelessness would put the entire family and estate at risk, and that he would be held accountable if anything were to happen.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was being dramatic for the sake of being dramatic, and that the local Mussulmans wouldn't dare attack a zamindar of his stature.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip was underestimating the situation and that the local Mussulmans had been making increasingly aggressive demands, which needed to be addressed promptly.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip sneered, telling Nikhil that he was more worried about the crops withering than any 'aggressive demands' from the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's voice rose in reprimand as he told Sandip that his carefree attitude was a threat to the entire region's stability.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snorted in derision, telling Nikhil that he was more concerned about his own dwindling fortunes than the supposed threats from the local Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that such levity was unbecoming of a zamindar, and that he expected a more serious consideration of the threats

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled and asked Nikhil if he was starting to believe in conspiracy theories again, adding that the local Mussulmans were hardly the stuff of midnight raids and torch-wielding mobs.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he was not one to indulge in baseless speculation, but the increasing tensions and the recent incidents in the neighboring village demanded attention and caution.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was being alarmist and that his own village was more at peace than ever, that the farmers were happy and the crops were thriving.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
